name: belian.earth
summary: Locally trained stocking indices (SI), performance benchmarks and ex-ante projections, with a low-cost view before any audit-grade commitment. All come with quantified uncertainty. belian.earth’s VM0047 product, ramet47, uses satellite embeddings to select reference areas that constrain the control plot donor region and define the SI model training extent. Reference areas are chosen where their whole satellite record up to the project start, and their spatial context, resemble the project’s, enhancing the reliability of control plot matches derived from the SI. ramet47 has independently reproduced the benchmark of the first issued VM0047 project (VCS 5511), within uncertainty bounds.
production: Our stocking index measures canopy structure, with NASA's GEDI lidar as the primary reference: canopy height (RH98) and plant area index (PAI), a measure of canopy density, used together. Where GEDI data is unavailable (beyond 51.6° N and 51.6° S), ICESat-2 ATL08 vegetation height data are used. It is built by fusing predictions from multiple satellite embedding products, including Embedded Seamless Data (Chen et al., 2026; Landsat and MODIS, 2000 to 2024), AlphaEarth Foundations (Brown et al., 2025; Sentinel-1/2, Landsat and GEDI, from 2017) and OlmoEarth v1.3 (Tseng et al., 2026; Sentinel-1/2 and Landsat, from 2017). Models are trained for the project's specific region against canopy measurements, ensuring better local accuracy. The derived SI is a gap-free 30 m series covering the project and reference areas for the 11 years before project start to the present; low-confidence pixel-years are down-weighted, not discarded. We map at 30 m because our models are trained on GEDI's 25 m lidar footprints, so a finer grid adds pixels, not information.
correlation: Canopy height and plant area index have a well-documented correlation with biomass, and combined they give a biomass proxy that correlates linearly with measured biomass across the biomes tested. The index is also checked against GEDI held out geographically, so the check area is never seen in training; against airborne-lidar canopy height in tropical forest and temperate forest (swisstopo); and by independently reproducing the benchmark of the first issued VM0047 project (VCS 5511). Accuracy figures are on our VM0047 page. Converting the index to biomass would add assumptions without adding anything the benchmark needs, and when we modelled biomass the same way it was less precise. That conversion needs to be done with ground-truth data from the project's own plots, and we can provide it as a separate service where needed.
limits: We provide the stocking index where its link to biomass can be shown for the project's forest type and ecoregion, and so far that link has held in every biome we have tested. It is a relative measure, which is what the VM0047 performance benchmark uses to compare the project with its controls. Absolute tonnes need field plots, and calibrating to a project's own plots is available as a separate service.
limitations: Saturation: in tall, dense tropical forest the satellite signal saturates for every product, and that sensor limit cannot be removed. Training for the project's region reduces the modelling part, where predictions are pulled towards an average, and from 2019, once GEDI enters the AlphaEarth embeddings, the gap to airborne lidar narrows. GEDI canopy height sits about 5 to 6 m above airborne-lidar height; this is absorbed in calibration. Earlier years, especially before 2013, are less certain and are down-weighted.
deliveryNoApi: Direct download from app.belian.earth: the reference areas, the stocking index, the dynamic baseline and performance benchmark, the uncertainty, and the audit pack. A view gives the same analysis and the same answer in the app, without the audit materials. Audit materials are also provided through Verra's Project Hub.

name: CYCLOPS
summary: CYCLOPS provides the annual aboveground-biomass mapping used as the stocking index under VM0047, together with the analysis built on it: eligible-area and historical-disturbance screening, donor-pool construction and automated control-plot matching, dynamic baseline and performance-benchmark calculation, uncertainty-deduction calculation, non permanence assessment and supporting text and figures for the PDD and monitoring report. The underlying foundation model and AGB are described in the publications below. CYCLOPS is US-incorporated and runs on dClimate’s EarthOS data infrastructure.
production: Two AGB products are built on these representations. (a) GEDI-trained; a scaling factor converts modelled relative height differences to AGB (t/ha). (b) Reference-calibrated representations are calibrated directly against AGB derived from airborne LiDAR or in-situ plots. Tree crowns are detected and segmented from a canopy height model, per-tree height and crown diameter extracted, and tree-level AGB. No scaling factor is applied. Where both are available, the reference-calibrated product is used.
correlation: Published validation (Atzberger et al. 2025, Remote Sensing of Environment) includes a chronosequence of 38 in-situ reference measurements across agroforestry plots of differing age classes, and comparison against gridded GEDI AGB products. Stratification is applied at ecoregion or biome level, depending on landscape diversity and the size of the available donor pool. Hold-out data are re-evaluated annually.
limits: Correlation is assessed at plot level (<1 ha) against reference AGB withheld from calibration. Where R² falls below 0.6, delivery is suspended and the model is re-calibrated against additional reference data, or the affected strata are excluded from delivery. VM0047 requires a positive, statistically significant relationship; we do not release an SI that cannot demonstrate one.
resolution: 10 m from 2017 (Sentinel-2) and 30 m for earlier years (Landsat)
years: Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 are used from 2017 onward; Landsat is used for earlier years.
limitations: GEDI orbital coverage spans approximately 51.6°N to 51.6°S; the GEDI-trained product is limited to that band, with ICESat-2 used beyond it. The reference-calibrated product requires client-supplied ALS or in-situ plot data. Geolocation offset between reference data and satellite pixels is a known source of residual error at plot scale. Against in-situ measurements the SI is close to linear to roughly 150 t/ha, with limited saturation to approximately 200 t/ha when compared with GEDI L4B; sensitivity declines above that range. Pre-2017 estimates rely on Landsat at coarser resolution.
deliveryNoApi: Delivered as: annual AGB raster (COG GeoTIFF); per-plot SI time series for project and matched control plots, in the project/control plot database format VM0047 requires; documentation of SI derivation; and a PDD/monitoring report. Project Hub API integration is in progress; until it completes, delivery is by secure transfer.

name: Lobelia Earth
summary:
A climate intelligence company combining Earth observation, predictive climate modelling, and advanced AI to turn complex planetary data into actionable decisions, backed by technology validated across premier European space and climate programs (ESA, Copernicus, ECMWF).
For VM0047, it supplies yearly 10m maps of aboveground biomass, canopy height, and canopy cover (2016 to present) with uncertainty ranges, delivered via API with automated project-control plot matching.
production: A biome-aware deep-learning (UNet) model fuses airborne lidar and GEDI with Sentinel-1/2, land cover and DEM data to map AGB, canopy height and canopy cover at 10 m each year from 2016. Imagery is restricted to region-specific growing seasons with under 30% cloud cover; clouds, shadows and snow are masked (SCL) and a yearly median composite is built. Outputs include 5th-95th percentile uncertainty.
correlation: Peer-reviewed validation (Perpinya-Valles et al., 2025) in four biomes gives Pearson r of 0.61-0.77. Per project, SI is benchmarked against local GEDI L4A footprints, cross-validated with national forest inventory data or project field plots, and explainable-AI analysis shows which sensors matter locally. SI is delivered only where correlation is statistically verified.
limits: Potential limitations can be assessed and discussed on a case-by-case basis with Lobelia science team.
limitations: Pearson r of 0.61-0.77 against reference data in the validation study (four biomes), so uncertainty is material; it is reported as 5th and 95th percentile confidence intervals.
deliveryNoApi: Via Lobelia's own API (job-based): outputs at three levels (raw yearly rasters, plot-level and reporting-level metrics), written to Lobelia's S3 bucket or the client's bucket.

name: TerraCarbon
summary: Advisory firm that helps develop carbon projects for natural climate solutions, from early feasibility to registration and monitoring. For VM0047 it builds a project-specific stocking index, matches project and control plots, and delivers a traceable performance benchmark.
production: Annual composites of Landsat, Sentinel-2 or HLS (SAR if optical is unavailable) over a 10-year history and a 100 km buffer, using the most cloud-free 3 months (widened to 6 if needed). A stocking index suited to the forest type is built from them, e.g., NDFI plus a disturbance-age model, and checked against field data where possible. Plots are about 3x3 pixel groups.
correlation: Case by case, using field data from the project area or ecoregion whenever possible. In an illustrative Brazilian eucalyptus case, an NDFI + disturbance-age model reached R2 of about 0.80-0.84 against stem-volume plots. Optical and SAR saturation is assessed per project.
limitations: Optical data saturate within 1-3 years in eucalyptus plantations; L-band SAR saturates at about 100-200 t/ha; the SI metric is therefore chosen project by project.
deliveryNoApi: To client and VVB: matching criteria, SI time-series raster, matched project/control plots, Excel workbook, written description and R/Python code.

name: Treefera
summary: AI-native intelligence platform for agricultural and soft-commodity supply chains, including forest cover, biomass and carbon. For VM0047 it provides an annual NDVI stocking index from Landsat (30 m, since 2000), an ARR eligibility checker, and performance monitoring and benchmarking.
production: NDVI is computed per pixel from Landsat 5/7/8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance (Microsoft Planetary Computer). Scenes up to 80% cloud are kept, clouds and shadows are masked with the QA band, same-day tiles are mosaicked, and each cell's annual value is the mean of valid pixels at 30 m (2000 to latest year, 2012 excluded). A harmonic regression then separates seasonal cycles from trend.
correlation: NDVI has a peer-reviewed correlation with AGB. For each project we show three lines of evidence: published NDVI-AGB relationships for the biome; proponent field plots used to cross-validate at plot-footprint scale; and independent AGB references where available. Correlation is reported with uncertainty. It weakens in high-biomass closed-canopy forest, which we flag.
limits: Needs at least 10 years of pre-start history and 30 project plots (0.81 ha each); 2012 is treated as missing; NDVI saturates in high-biomass closed-canopy forest (flagged).
limitations: NDVI saturates in closed-canopy forest; Landsat only (Sentinel-2 under evaluation); 2012 missing; Table A1 overlays not applied; Step 4 control revalidation not implemented.
deliveryNoApi: Verra Project Hub, Treefera App and API

name: TransparenC
summary: Geospatial analytics for carbon markets: 100+ automated data layers for feasibility, due diligence and digital MRV. For VM0047 it supplies stocking index data (AGB or EVI) and a dynamic baseline built from a donor zone and matched control pixels.
production:
AGB (10 m): A regional neural network maps AlphaEarth embeddings to quality-filtered GEDI L4A footprint AGB. Outputs include a calibrated 90% prediction interval per pixel and a project-total standard error.

NDFI (30 m): Annual composites of Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance, cloud- and shadow-masked with the QA band and harmonised across sensors. Each project uses a fixed, biome-specific peak growing-season window of at least four months, the same every year. NDFI has no per-pixel uncertainty.
correlation: AGB: Accuracy (RMSE, Mg/ha) is reported for each request. NDFI: the relationship with AGB is fitted against proponent field plots or, where these are unavailable, quality-filtered GEDI L4A footprints; R², RMSE and bias are reported.
years: AGB: 2017–latest complete year. NDFI: 2000–latest complete year (2012 excluded).
updateFrequency: Annual. Optional sub-annual monitoring on request.
limitations: NDFI saturates in closed, high-biomass canopies and is sensitive to phenology. AGB is available only from 2017 onward. Landsat 7 scan-line gaps (from 2003) and missing 2012 data reduce quality in early years.
deliveryNoApi: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs, Parquet tables and JSON summaries, downloaded from signed links, with code and model versions recorded. Dynamic baseline jobs also include an interactive map viewer and a methods report.

name: Varaha
summary:
Varaha is Asia's largest nature-based carbon project developer. We work with 200,000+
smallholder farmers and nearly 1 million hectares under management across South and
Southeast Asia and West Africa, and ARR and agroforestry are where our experience
runs deepest.
Smallholder land is hard to monitor from space: plots are small and monsoon clouds are
persistent. So we don't rely on one sensor. Our MRV stack fuses optical and radar
satellite data with machine learning and field plots, and turns them into tree-cover,
land-use and biomass datasets built for VM0047.
production:
Varaha’s Stocking Index is the Cross-Sensor Vegetative Index (CSVI), a weighted
fusion of NDVI and normalised SAR cross-polarised backscatter. Baseline years use
monthly median Landsat 5/7/8 NDVI with annual ALOS PALSAR/PALSAR-2 L-band HV
(weights 0.6/0.4). Monitoring uses co-registered Sentinel-2 L2A NDVI with Sentinel-1
VH, weights selected against field AGB. CSVI avoids the stacked model errors and
NDVI saturation that limit CHM, AGB and NDFI products. CSVI works directly on
calibrated satellite signals, using optical data for canopy greenness and SAR for woody
structure. Globally, Seasonal Window (non monsoon season) has been set for each
agro-ecological zone to remove cloud-affected scenes and other local geological
factors.
correlation: Four steps: classify the project ecoregion and forest type; establish project-specific sample plots (tree inventory converted to plot AGB with local allometry); fit a project-specific SI-AGB regression with k-fold and spatially-blocked cross-validation (R2, RMSE, MAE, bias, residual diagnostics); benchmark against literature and propagate uncertainty. A validation report accompanies each SI.
limits:
Field-validated for South Asian plantations and agroforestry (AGB 5–70 t/ha); Global
coverage with local ground truth calibration and validation. CSVI is a relative index for
performance benchmarking, not an AGB estimate. Weights vary by vegetation type.
limitations:
Persistent monsoon cloud (mitigated by dry-season compositing and SAR) and
topographic shadow in mountains (DEM correction, residual uncertainty reported).
Sparse crowns at 8–10 m spacing reduce sensitivity. Baseline (L-band PALSAR) and
monitoring (C-band Sentinel-1) sensors differ.
deliveryNoApi:
SI delivered with metadata, valid-pixel counts, quality flags and a project-specific
SI-AGB validation report. Per-plot CSVI time series for project and control plots, with
weight settings, SDM match tables, control-plot weights, PBt per monitoring cycle and a
field-validation report.

name: Kanop
summary: Kanop helps project developers build and monitor ARR projects under VM0047. Our team runs the full benchmarking workflow for you: eligibility, stocking index time series, dynamic performance benchmark and control plot selection, ex-ante estimates, and PDD drafting, then supports you through validation and verification. The data comes from Kanop’s deep-learning models, which map aboveground biomass globally at 10 m and 30 m from satellite imagery and LiDAR.
production:
Kanop’s deep-learning model predicts aboveground biomass density (Mg/ha) each year from multi-sensor satellite composites. It is trained on about 125 Mha of LiDAR reference data, combining airborne LiDAR and GEDI.

* 30 m product (2000-2025): Landsat-7, Landsat-8, Landsat-9, ALOS PALSAR L-band radar, and SRTM elevation
* 10 m product (2017-2025): adds Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2
Composites favour dry-season observations where available, and optical imagery goes through enhanced cloud masking. This keeps the time series consistent from year to year and maximises coverage, including in persistently cloudy tropical regions.
correlation: SI is AGB itself (Mg/ha). The model is trained on about 125 Mha of structural reference data (42 Mha airborne LiDAR, 83 Mha GEDI); global site-level validation gives R2 0.65 against LiDAR-derived AGB. Optional project recalibration with field measurements (Gaussian Process Regression fusion, inverse-variance weighting) gives a default 95% confidence interval.
limits: 30 m product (2000-2025): Landsat-7, Landsat-8, Landsat-9, ALOS PALSAR L-band radar, and SRTM elevation
resolution: 10 m product (2017-2025): adds Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2
updateFrequency: Composites favour dry-season observations where available, and optical imagery goes through enhanced cloud masking. This keeps the time series consistent from year to year and maximises coverage, including in persistently cloudy tropical regions.

name: Chloris
summary: Chloris uses machine learning on multi-satellite data to estimate aboveground biomass stock, biomass change and forest cover change. For VM0047 it supplies an annual AGBD stocking index (2000-2025) and a full dynamic baselining workflow.
production: Landsat acquisitions are aligned to a fixed 30 m grid, corrected to NBAR reflectance, and masked with the Landsat QA layer plus a custom cloud mask. A machine-learning model (Baccini et al. method) predicts AGBD using all imagery in the target year plus context from previous and subsequent years. Maps are reprojected to a regional equal-area projection, keeping 30 m pixels.
correlation: Validated against independent reference data in the United States and the Brazilian Amazon: NEON field plots, 38 site means (R² = 0.75); USFS FIA inventory, state-level means 2003–2025 (R² = 0.90, mean bias +13 Mg/ha); airborne-lidar biomass (Ometto et al. 2023), eight Amazon states (R² = 0.49–0.90 by state). These compare area means, not single pixels. Across Brazilian states, biomass trends correlate with GEDI canopy-height trends (r = 0.76). Calibration against project field data is available as a separate engagement.
limits: No technical limits. Terms and conditions apply to the use of data, as per license agreement.
limitations: Independent validation figures refer to area means (sites, states, lidar transects), not single 30 m pixels; per-pixel uncertainty is delivered with the data. Absolute stocks can show regional biases against field inventories. In persistently cloudy regions fewer clear Landsat observations are available, and some cloud contamination can remain after masking. The record starts in 2000, so projects that started before 2010 have less than ten years of pre-start history.
deliveryNoApi: REST API and data deliverable downloads. VM0047 engagements include the following deliverables: a report detailing the exact methodology used for the analysis (formats: .docx and PDF), SDM and Performance Benchmark table files (format: csv), and georeferenced files containing stocking index time series for site plots and matched control plots (format: gpkg).

name: Treeconomy Ltd.
summary: Treeconomy combines remote sensing, AI and ecological science to provide forest carbon data. For VM0047, it supplies satellite-based stocking index data and supports dynamic performance benchmarking, site eligibility assessments and carbon projections.
production: Treeconomy’s Satellite-Only Biomass Model (SB10) combines annual AlphaEarth satellite embeddings with elevation, ecoregion and land-cover data. A machine-learning model calibrated against NASA GEDI biomass observations produces annual biomass maps on a fixed 10 m grid. GEDI reference observations are filtered to regional seasonal windows. The model uses locally adaptive conformal prediction to estimate uncertainty.
correlation: Treeconomy reports validation for its Integrated Biomass Model (IB10), combining spaceborne lidar and ground data. At Gashaka Gumti National Park, reported Pearson correlations were 0.54 against independent GEDI footprints and 0.43 against ground plots. Project-specific calibration uses partner-supplied forest inventory plots, with out-of-sample cross-validation reporting RMSE and bias. These results are described for IB10, not explicitly for SB10.

name: Space Intelligence
summary: Space Intelligence is an Edinburgh-based company that supplies audit-grade nature data from satellites to corporations, developers and Verra. For each VM0047 project, it builds a site-specific stocking index from suitable imagery, tests it against above-ground biomass, and supplies it to proponents.
production: For every VM0047 project, Space Intelligence develops a bespoke, site-specific remote sensing stocking index. These normally use synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite data, typically from the European Space Agency (ESA), NASA and/or the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), though occasionally optical satellite data is used. Several possible stocking indices are tested, and the one with the best relationship to above-ground biomass for the project's ecosystem is selected.
correlation: If a project has forest inventory plots, candidate indices are tested against above-ground biomass from those plots. Space Intelligence can support field protocol design and data collection. Where no plots exist, it uses open forest plots, regional or national forest inventory data, or relationships from peer-reviewed studies (e.g. Mitchard 2009, 2012; Bouvet 2018) to develop a suitable stocking index. Fit statistics and data sources are reported for each project.
limits: Stocking indices can be provided for any project eligible under VM0047, without regional restriction. For each forest type, various stocking indices are tested to find the one most appropriate to the forest type and project.
resolution: 10 m to 25 m, depending on the satellite data behind each project's stocking index. Sentinel-1, NISAR and Sentinel-2 (where optical data is used) have a 10 m pixel size. ALOS PALSAR-2/4 has a 25 m pixel size.
years: 2007 to present. Coverage starts with the ALOS PALSAR archive; the satellite used for each project depends on the most suitable stocking index. The archive covers baseline years for projects starting from 2016.
limitations: Space Intelligence mostly uses SAR data, which is not impacted by clouds and is less impacted by herbaceous vegetation than optical data. SAR backscatter saturates at high biomass and is sensitive to moisture, so dry-season scenes are used where relevant.
deliveryNoApi: Delivered to the proponent: yearly GeoTIFF stocking index maps, project and control plot files, and a detailed analyst-written PDF report justifying the index selection.
